updates.name: Debra P.C. Peters
updates.bio: USDA-ARS ecologist at the Jornada Experimental Range. The Jornada LTER profile describes research on how global change alters ecosystem dynamics at multiple scales, ecotones, spatially explicit simulation models and cross-scale interactions, and lists roles as Jornada lead scientist (2002-2010), Jornada Basin LTER lead PI from 2003, EcoTrends co-lead and Ecosphere editor-in-chief.
updates.research_interests: global change effects on ecosystem dynamics across spatial scales; boundary and ecotone dynamics; spatially explicit ecosystem simulation modeling; nonlinear spatial and temporal dynamics; catastrophic events; cross-scale interactions
updates.current_affiliation: USDA Agricultural Research Service, Jornada Experimental Range
updates.evidence: Debra Peters Ecologist, USDA-ARS, Jornada Experimental Range Primary Research Interests
updates.notes: Bio source is the Jornada Basin LTER person page (200), which is undated and whose listed activities run to 2016, so the lead-PI and editor roles are stated as the page gives them and may be historical (lternet.edu now lists Niall Hanan as JRN lead PI, per batch R-PEOPLE2-ARID-NM-01a). jornada.nmsu.edu/people/debra-peters (200, existing homepage) shows only 'Ecologist'. Status left null: neither page says active/former, and the lake's 'former' could not be re-sourced. ORCID: registry search found 0000-0002-5842-8099 'Debra Peters' (Scopus/Loop ids, no employment entry; institutions listed are CSU, Iowa State, SDSU, AAAS, ESA); no USDA-ARS/Jornada employment and no fetched official page links it, so not recorded. Verifier: bio reworded to break a 7-word run copied from the source.

updates.name: Stephen K. Hamilton
updates.bio: Ecosystem ecologist and biogeochemist whose work centers on water in wetlands, streams, lakes, reservoirs and watersheds, and on how cropping systems affect water and climate. Long a professor at MSU's Kellogg Biological Station and a KBS LTER principal investigator, he retired from MSU and from Cary Institute as of 2024 but remains academically active.
updates.research_interests: wetlands; streams, rivers and lakes; agricultural ecology; water quality; tropical rivers; floodplains; nutrient cycling and greenhouse gas emissions
updates.current_title: Retired Professor (MSU Kellogg Biological Station); former Senior Scientist, Cary Institute
updates.current_affiliation: Michigan State University / Cary Institute of Ecosystem Studies (retired)
updates.evidence: As of 2024, Hamilton is retired from both Cary Institute and from his long-time position as a Professor at Michigan State University
updates.notes: Existing homepage lter.kbs.msu.edu/people/faculty/stephen-k-hamilton/ returns 404; replaced by the Cary Institute profile (200). Cary page says he was a principal investigator for the NSF LTER site at MSU and a GLBRC project leader. His Cary CV (caryinstitute.org/sites/default/files/public/downloads/bio/hamilton.pdf, 200) dates MSU retirement to Jan 2023. ltar.ars.usda.gov/sites/kbs/ (200) still lists 'Steve Hamilton' among KBS LTAR leaders, so the current co-PI affiliation may be stale; flag for a research batch. Existing ORCID confirmed at pub.orcid.org: name Stephen Hamilton; employments Cary Institute Senior Scientist (2018-) and Michigan State University Kellogg Biological Station Professor (1995-). No Google Scholar profile link on the Cary page (only per-paper Scholar search links).

updates.name: Martha H. Conklin
updates.bio: Professor of Engineering at UC Merced, among its founding faculty in 2003. She studies groundwater-surface water interactions, reaction timescales and stream solute transport using natural tracers, lately in montane headwater catchments, and has been co-PI of the Sierra Nevada Critical Zone Observatory at the Kings River Experimental Watershed, leading meadow water and nutrient budget research.
updates.research_interests: groundwater-surface water interactions; natural tracers and reaction timescales; dissolved constituent transport in streams; montane meadow water and nutrient budgets; snowmelt hydrology and evapotranspiration; water quality
updates.evidence: Dr. Conklin is Co-PI of the National Science Foundation's Sierra Nevada Critical Zone Observatory located at the Kings River Experimental Watershed
updates.notes: Existing homepage es.ucmerced.edu/people/martha-conklin returns 403 (also via WebFetch); used her UC Merced faculty site faculty.ucmerced.edu/mconklin/ (200), which is undated and likely older, so the CZO co-PI role may be historical. Status not stated.

updates.name: Roger C. Bales
updates.bio: Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Engineering and founding faculty member at UC Merced, also adjunct in civil and environmental engineering at UC Berkeley, continuing research through recall appointments. He formerly directed the Sierra Nevada Research Institute and Southern Sierra Critical Zone Observatory; his work now targets California water supply and ecosystem adaptation to climate warming.
updates.research_interests: ecosystem climate solutions; water resources; mountain hydrology; climate communications

updates.bio: Kansas State University plant and landscape ecologist (PhD, University of Arkansas, 1985) whose Division of Biology page gives the title Professor and Director of Konza Prairie Biological Station. Research focus: fire and grazing in grasslands, woody plant expansion into grasslands, human influences on ecosystems, remote sensing and GIS in ecosystem research, and ecological data management.

updates.name: Melinda D. Smith
updates.bio: University Distinguished Professor of Biology and Vice Provost for Faculty Affairs at Colorado State University. A plant community ecologist working mostly in the field on grassland diversity, species abundance and links to ecosystem function in Central Great Plains shortgrass, mixedgrass and tallgrass prairies, with collaborators in South African and Inner Mongolian grasslands.
updates.research_interests: plant community ecology; patterns, determinants and dynamics of diversity and species abundance; diversity and ecosystem function; grassland ecosystems of the Central Great Plains
updates.current_title: Vice Provost for Faculty Affairs and University Distinguished Professor, Department of Biology
updates.evidence: Melinda D. Smith Vice Provost for Faculty Affairs and University Distinguished Professor in the Department of Biology
